lingo-more:0.note: MW lob: a soft high-arching shot, throw, or kick

lingo-more:1.note: dictionary.com daisy-cutter, Collins British: soccer, a powerful shot that moves close to the ground

lingo-more:10.note: MW goal line: line at either end on which a goal is situated

lingo-more:11.note: MW center circle: circle at the center of a playing surface where a kickoff takes place

lingo-more:12.note: dictionary.com crossbar: the horizontal bar forming part of the goal posts, as in soccer. post is not among the wrong answers

lingo-more:13.note: MW post: goalpost. crossbar is not among the wrong answers

lingo-more:14.note: dictionary.com technical area, Collins British: soccer, area at the side of the pitch to which managers, trainers, coaches are restricted

lingo-more:15.note: MW midfield: the portion of a playing field midway between goals

lingo-more:16.note: MW goalie: a player who defends the goal (as in soccer) : goalkeeper

lingo-more:17.note: dictionary.com skipper: a captain or leader, as of a team

lingo-more:18.note: MW linesman: an official who assists a referee, especially on out-of-bounds or offside. dictionary.com (Collins) also says helps the referee. Neither entry says on the sideline, so the means goes past the source

lingo-more:19.note: MW halfback: a player stationed immediately behind the forward line (as in soccer)

lingo-more:2.note: MW pile driver: a forceful hit or kick (as of a ball)

lingo-more:20.note: dictionary.com utility player, Collins British: a player capable of playing competently in any of several positions

lingo-more:21.note: MW defender: a player in a sport assigned to a defensive position

fix.means: Mom who takes her kids to soccer

lingo-more:22.note: MW soccer mom: a mother who accompanies her children to their soccer games. The entry says accompanies, not drives

lingo-more:23.note: MW ball girl: a female attendant who retrieves balls for players or officials (examples are tennis, baseball, basketball but the sense is general)

lingo-more:24.note: MW scout: a person sent to watch players in action with a view to recommending their acquisition

lingo-more:25.note: MW free agent: a professional athlete free to negotiate a contract with any team

lingo-more:26.note: MW onside: not offside, in a position legally to play or receive the ball

lingo-more:27.note: MW kickoff says only a kick that puts the ball into play. dictionary.com kickoff (soccer sense) says it puts a stationary ball into play from the center line at the start or after a goal has been scored, which shows the sentence

lingo-more:28.note: MW throw-in: a throw made from the touchline in soccer to put the ball back in play

lingo-more:29.note: MW goal kick: awarded to the defense when the ball goes over the end line off an opposing player

lingo-more:3.note: dictionary.com inswinger, Collins British: soccer, a ball kicked, esp from a corner, so as to curve towards the goal

lingo-more:30.note: dictionary.com wall: soccer, a line of defenders standing shoulder to shoulder to block a free kick

lingo-more:31.note: MW professional foul: a foul made on purpose especially to prevent the other team from scoring a goal

lingo-more:32.note: MW drop ball: putting a soccer ball in play by dropping it after a temporary suspension

lingo-more:33.note: M-W halftime: an intermission between halves of a game or contest. No wrong answer fits “At ___”

lingo-more:34.note: Dictionary.com full time, Collins British noun 2: the end of a football or other match. halftime is not among its wrong answers

lingo-more:35.note: Dictionary.com knockout, Collins British: a competition in which competitors are eliminated progressively

lingo-more:36.note: Dictionary.com kickabout: a casual game of soccer, primarily played as a way to pass time

lingo-more:37.note: Dictionary.com five-a-side, Collins British: a version of soccer with five players on each side

lingo-more:38.note: M-W bye: the position of a participant in a tournament who advances to the next round without playing

lingo-more:39.note: M-W rematch: a second match between the same contestants or teams. playoff is not among its wrong answers

lingo-more:4.note: dictionary.com half volley, Collins British verb: to hit or kick a ball immediately after it bounces

lingo-more:40.note: M-W playoff: a final contest to determine the winner between contestants or teams that have tied. rematch is not among its wrong answers

lingo-more:41.note: M-W shutout: a game or contest in which one side fails to score

lingo-more:42.note: M-W goalless: having no goal scored by either team

lingo-more:43.note: M-W squeaker: a contest (such as a game or an election) won by a small margin

lingo-more:44.note: M-W drubbing (under drub): to beat severely, to defeat decisively. blowout is not among its wrong answers

lingo-more:45.note: M-W blowout: an easy or one-sided victory. drubbing is not among its wrong answers

lingo-more:46.note: Dictionary.com silver goal, Collins British (soccer): a goal scored in a full half of extra time that counts as the winner if it is the only goal in that half

lingo-more:47.note: Dictionary.com away goal, Collins British: a goal scored by a team playing away from home, counting for more than home goals in certain competitions

lingo-more:48.note: Dictionary.com route one, Collins British (soccer): a style of play involving long high kicks towards a central striker

lingo-more:49.note: Dictionary.com total football, Collins British: no fixed positions and every outfield player can join in the attack

lingo-more:5.note: MW dropkick: dropping a ball and kicking it at the moment it starts to rebound

lingo-more:50.note: Dictionary.com back four, Collins British (soccer): the defensive players, usually two fullbacks and two centre backs

lingo-more:51.note: M-W man-to-man: a system of defense in which each defensive player guards a specified opponent

lingo-more:52.note: Dictionary.com tifo (Chiefly Soccer): a coordinated display by fans in the stadium, especially a large banner

lingo-more:53.note: Dictionary.com cap, Chiefly British: an instance of playing in an international game or match as part of a national team

lingo-more:54.note: M-W eleven: a football team. Dictionary.com eleven: a set or group of 11 people, such as a football or soccer team

lingo-more:55.note: Dictionary.com footy, Collins British: informal football

lingo-more:56.note: Dictionary.com giant killer, Collins British: a person, sports team, etc, that defeats an apparently superior opponent

lingo-more:57.note: Dictionary.com wooden spoon, Collins British: a booby prize, esp in sporting contests

lingo-more:58.note: M-W season ticket: a ticket (as to all of a club’s home games) valid during a specified time

lingo-more:59.note: M-W dribble: to propel by successive slight taps or bounces with hand, foot, or stick

lingo-more:6.note: MW punt: kick a soccer ball dropped from the hands before it hits the ground

lingo-more:60.note: M-W sky: to hit (a ball) high into the air. No wrong answer sends the ball over the crossbar

lingo-more:61.note: M-W net: to hit (a ball or puck) into the goal for a score (as in hockey or soccer)

lingo-more:62.note: M-W save: to prevent an opponent from scoring or winning, and the noun: a play that prevents an opponent from scoring

lingo-more:63.note: M-W tie: to equalize (the score) in a game or contest

lingo-more:64.note: M-W whitewash: to hold (an opponent) scoreless in a game or contest. mark, which would also fit, is not among its wrong answers

lingo-more:65.note: Dictionary.com mark, Collins British verb (sport): to stay close to (an opponent) to hamper his or her play

lingo-more:7.note: MW back pass: a pass to a player behind the ball carrier (as in soccer)

lingo-more:8.note: MW touchline: lines that bound the long sides of the field in soccer

lingo-more:9.note: MW penalty area shows the box in front of each goal but not the keeper’s hands. dictionary.com penalty-area (Collins British) says it is the area within which the goalkeeper may handle the ball, so that page supports both sentence and means

soccer:0.note: merriam-webster.com bicycle kick: kick in soccer executed by somersaulting backwards to strike the ball in midair

soccer:1.note: dictionary.com scissors kick (Collins, football): player leaps into the air raising one leg and brings up the other to kick the ball

soccer:10.note: dictionary.com chip (Collins, sport): a shot or kick lofted into the air, esp over an obstacle or an opposing player’s head

soccer:11.note: dictionary.com one-two (Collins, soccer): another term for wall pass, which dictionary.com/browse/wall-pass defines as passing to a teammate and sprinting forward to receive the quick return

soccer:12.note: dictionary.com Panenka: a penalty kick taken as a slow, gently arching shot to the center of goal

soccer:13.note: dictionary.com keepy-uppy (Collins, soccer): keeping a ball off the ground by bouncing it on a foot, knee or head

soccer:14.note: merriam-webster.com penalty kick: a free kick at the goal in soccer from a point 12 yards in front of the goal for certain violations. Free kick is rightly absent from the wrong answers

soccer:15.note: MW corner kick defines it as “a free kick from a corner of a soccer field awarded … when a defender plays the ball out-of-bounds over the end line.” Sentence and means are right, but by the deck’s own source free kick (a listed wrong answer) is also true in this blank, so group them

soccer:16.note: merriam-webster.com free kick: a kick with which an opponent may not interfere, awarded because of an infraction by an opponent

soccer:17.note: merriam-webster.com red card: shown to a player who broke the rules and will not be allowed to continue playing

soccer:18.note: merriam-webster.com yellow card: shown to a player who broke the rules and is being officially warned

soccer:19.note: merriam-webster.com offside: illegally in advance of the ball or puck

soccer:2.note: merriam-webster.com volley: a kick of the ball in soccer before it rebounds

soccer:20.note: dictionary.com handball (Collins, soccer): the offence of a player other than a keeper in his own area touching the ball with a hand. The Usage note there adds “hand or part of their arm”

soccer:21.note: dictionary.com dive (Soccer): a dramatic fall or feigned injury to get the opponent penalized, Collins: pretending to have been tripped to win a free kick or penalty

fix.ex: The striker waits near the other team’s goal, hoping to score

soccer:23.note: MW striker gives only “a forward in soccer.” dictionary.com/browse/striker (Collins, soccer) gives “an attacking player, esp one who generally positions himself near his opponent’s goal in the hope of scoring,” which supports the means line. Neither source supports “only job is to score” or “never helps on defense,” which is untrue of real strikers, so the sentence is reworded to the dictionary sense

soccer:24.note: merriam-webster.com center forward: someone who plays in the middle of the front line of players in soccer and other sports

soccer:25.note: merriam-webster.com winger: a player in a wing position, and merriam-webster.com/dictionary/wing: one of the offensive positions on either side of a center position

soccer:26.note: merriam-webster.com midfielder: a member of a midfield, and merriam-webster.com/dictionary/midfield: the portion of a playing field midway between goals. dictionary.com/browse/midfielder adds that midfielders play both offensively and defensively

soccer:27.note: merriam-webster.com fullback: a primarily defensive player usually stationed nearest the defended goal (as in soccer)

soccer:28.note: merriam-webster.com sweeper: a lone back in soccer who plays between the line of the defenders and the goal

soccer:29.note: MW playmaker only gives “a player who leads the offense for a team (as in basketball or hockey),” no soccer. dictionary.com/browse/playmaker (Collins, sport) gives “a player whose role is to create scoring opportunities for his or her team-mates,” which covers soccer and the sentence’s passes that set up goals

soccer:3.note: merriam-webster.com header: a shot or pass in soccer made by heading the ball

soccer:30.note: dictionary.com false nine (Soccer): a center forward who drops back into the midfield to receive the ball

soccer:31.note: dictionary.com target man (Collins, soccer): an attacking player to whom high crosses are played, esp a tall forward

soccer:32.note: dictionary.com gaffer: the coach or manager of a sports team

soccer:33.note: merriam-webster.com hat trick: the scoring of three goals in one game (as of hockey or soccer) by a single player

soccer:34.note: merriam-webster.com clean sheet: a game in which the opposing team is prevented from scoring

soccer:35.note: merriam-webster.com own goal: a goal in soccer that a player accidentally scores against his or her own team

soccer:36.note: merriam-webster.com equalizer: a score that ties a game

soccer:37.note: MW nil gives only “nothing at all : zero,” with nothing about scores. dictionary.com/browse/nil (Collins) gives “another word for nothing: used esp in the scoring of certain games,” which supports the means line

soccer:38.note: dictionary.com assist (Collins noun, sport): a pass or other action by a player which enables another player to score a goal

soccer:39.note: merriam-webster.com shoot-out: a shooting competition in overtime to decide a game (as in soccer) tied at the end of regular play

soccer:4.note: merriam-webster.com banana kick: kick striking the side of the ball that makes it curve laterally in the air

soccer:40.note: merriam-webster.com sudden death: extra play to break a tie in which the first to score wins

soccer:41.note: dictionary.com golden goal (Collins, soccer): the first goal scored in extra time, which wins the match

soccer:42.note: merriam-webster.com injury time: time added at the end of a game of soccer because of time lost when players are injured. Stoppage time is rightly absent from the wrong answers

soccer:43.note: dictionary.com stoppage time (Collins, sport): another name for injury time. Injury time is rightly absent from the wrong answers

soccer:44.note: merriam-webster.com friendly (noun): a match between sports teams that has no connection with league or championship play

soccer:45.note: merriam-webster.com derby: a game between local sports teams

soccer:46.note: merriam-webster.com futsal: a game developed from soccer typically played indoors between two teams of five players

soccer:47.note: merriam-webster.com howler: a humorous and ridiculous blunder

soccer:48.note: merriam-webster.com sitter: an easy scoring or fielding chance

soccer:49.note: dictionary.com tap-in (Collins, soccer): a goal scored without great effort by knocking the ball in from close range

soccer:5.note: merriam-webster.com backheel: a kick of the ball backward with the heel

soccer:50.note: merriam-webster.com clinical: done or performed with excellence and precision

soccer:51.note: merriam-webster.com set piece: a carefully planned sequence of movements performed by a team (as in soccer). dictionary.com/browse/set-piece names a corner kick as the example

soccer:52.note: dictionary.com tiki-taka (Soccer): keeping possession and moving upfield through a series of quick, short passes

soccer:53.note: dictionary.com gegenpressing (Soccer): on losing the ball, immediately seeking repossession with aggressive pressure

soccer:54.note: dictionary.com relegate (Collins): to demote a football team to a lower division

soccer:6.note: merriam-webster.com cross: an attacking pass in soccer played across the field from one side to the other or to the middle

soccer:7.note: dictionary.com nutmeg (Collins verb, sport): to kick or hit the ball between the legs of an opposing player

soccer:8.note: dictionary.com stepover (Collins): raising the foot over the ball while in possession to wrong-foot an opponent

soccer:9.note: dictionary.com dummy (Collins): a feigned pass or move in a sport such as football or rugby
